newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle trade light at $63 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle trade light at $63 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. feedlot cattle in Kansas on Monday sold at $63.00 per cwt in light volume, unchanged from the bulk of last week's trade in the central and southern Plains, feedlot sources said.
About 2,000 steers and heifers, mostly heifers, like to grade select and choice, sold in Kansas, they said. No sales were reported in the Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma area.
Bids most of the day ranged from $62.00 to $63.00 and were mostly passed by owners pricing cattle at $64.00 to $65.00, cattle feeders said.

Fed cattle prices were seen underpinned by firm demand from packers buying cattle for a full slaughter schedule next week, sources said. This week was expected to be a short week as the industry winds down for the Independence Day holiday on Friday, they said. Prices were seen underpinned by spillover strength from sharply higher hog prices.
Prices also could be bolstered by expected showlists near last week's level.
However, prices could be eroded by sluggish beef demand this week, with retailers said to be well stocked for the holiday, sources said.
